library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("vandenBerg_2025_natalizumab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("vandenBerg_2025_natalizumab"))$description`
* Article: [CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol 2025;14(6):1032-1041](https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70014) (open access, PMC12167911). The Supporting Information contains the final NONMEM control stream (Section 6) and the full parameter table (Table S4).

Van den Berg et al. developed a population PK model of intravenous
natalizumab, an anti-alpha4-integrin monoclonal antibody, in patients with
relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) on maintenance treatment, and
used it to evaluate model-informed precision dosing (MIPD) of the dosing
interval against a decision-tree protocol driven by therapeutic drug
monitoring. The final model has two compartments with parallel linear and
Michaelis-Menten (target-mediated) elimination from the central compartment.
Body weight scales linear clearance and central volume as estimated power
functions normalised to 70 kg; intercompartmental clearance is fixed to
0.4 L/day from an earlier natalizumab model (Muralidharan 2017).

# Population

The model was fitted to 2523 serum natalizumab concentrations (2489 troughs
and 34 peaks drawn 1 h after infusion) from 379 RRMS patients treated at 20
clinics in the Netherlands (van den Berg 2025 Table 1, Table S1). Median weight
was 73 kg (IQR 64-83), median height 174 cm (IQR 168-180), median age 38 years
(IQR 32-47), and 78.6% were female. Data were pooled from the STDMS biobank
cohort (standard 4-week interval), the PDNMS trial (NCT03516526) and the two
NEXTMS arms (NCT04225312) whose personalised extended intervals targeted
troughs of 10 ug/mL (main) or 5 ug/mL (low). Every dose was 300 mg IV; the
median dose interval was 35 days (range 21-64). Patients with anti-drug
antibodies were excluded. Race was not reported.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("vandenBerg_2025_natalizumab")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every value is also recorded as an in-file comment next to the matching `ini()`
entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/vandenBerg_2025_natalizumab.R`. "Section 6"
is the final-model NONMEM control stream in the Supporting Information.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Two-compartment IV model, parallel linear + Michaelis-Menten elimination from central | n/a | Results "Two-Compartment PK Model"; Section 6 `$DES` |
| Saturable rate `Vmax * C / (Km + C)` with `C = A(1) / V1` | n/a | Supplement Section 2 equation; Section 6 `$DES` |
| `lcl` | log(0.164 L/day) | Table 2 / Table S4 `CL`; THETA(1) |
| `lvc` | log(3.48 L) | Table 2 / Table S4 `Vc`; THETA(2) |
| `lvp` | log(3.48 L) | Table 2 / Table S4 `Vp`; THETA(3) |
| `lq` | fixed(log(0.4 L/day)) | Table 2 `Q` (Fixed); Section 6 `Q = 0.4` |
| `lvmax` | log(2.86 mg/day) | Table 2 / Table S4 `Vmax`; THETA(4) |
| `lkm` | log(0.875 mg/L) | Table 2 / Table S4 `Km`; THETA(5) |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.6 | Table 2 `WT on CL`; THETA(7) |
| `e_wt_vc` | 0.26 | Table 2 `WT on Vc`; THETA(8) |
| Weight form `(WT/70)^theta` on CL and V1 | n/a | Table 2 footnote; Section 6 `$PK` |
| `etalcl` | 0.050678 (22.8% CV) | Table 2 IIV CL |
| `etalvp` | 0.094605 (31.5% CV) | Table 2 IIV Vp |
| `etalvmax` | 0.065413 (26% CV) | Table 2 IIV Vmax |
| No IIV on Vc, Q, Km | n/a | Section 6 `$PK`; Supplement Section 4 |
| `propSd` | 0.22 | Table 2 proportional error 22 CV%; Section 6 `W = SQRT(THETA(6)**2*IPRED**2)` |

The IIV variances use omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2). The Supplement says the CV was
computed "as described elsewhere" (Mould and Upton 2012); Table S6 confirms the
log-normal form, because its mean cross-validation variances (0.0512, 0.102,
0.0652) give exactly the cross-validation CVs printed in Table 2 (22.9%,
32.8%, 26.0%) under that formula.

```{r omega-check}
cv_from_omega <- function(omega2) 100 * sqrt(exp(omega2) - 1)
xval <- tibble(
  Parameter = c("CL", "Vp", "Vmax"),
  `Table S6 mean omega^2` = c(0.0512, 0.102, 0.0652),
  `Table 2 cross-validation CV%` = c(22.9, 32.8, 26.0)
) |>
  mutate(`CV% from omega^2` = cv_from_omega(`Table S6 mean omega^2`))
knitr::kable(xval, digits = 2)
stopifnot(all(abs(xval$`CV% from omega^2` - xval$`Table 2 cross-validation CV%`) < 0.15))
```

# Weight effect sizes

The paper reports that weight changes clearance by a factor of 0.85-1.34 and
central volume by 0.93-1.14 between the 2.5th and 97.5th weight percentiles
(Results). Inverting each ratio through its own exponent must recover the same
pair of weights for both parameters if the two exponents were transcribed
correctly.

```{r effect-size}
mod <- readModelDb("vandenBerg_2025_natalizumab")
ini_vals <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta
wt_from_ratio <- function(ratio, exponent) 70 * ratio^(1 / exponent)
eff <- tibble(
  Percentile = c("2.5th", "97.5th"),
  `CL ratio` = c(0.85, 1.34),
  `Vc ratio` = c(0.93, 1.14)
) |>
  mutate(
    `Weight implied by CL (kg)` = wt_from_ratio(`CL ratio`, ini_vals[["e_wt_cl"]]),
    `Weight implied by Vc (kg)` = wt_from_ratio(`Vc ratio`, ini_vals[["e_wt_vc"]])
  )
knitr::kable(eff, digits = 2)
# The Vc ratios are printed to two decimals on a 0.26 exponent, so each
# implied weight carries a few kg of rounding; a swapped or mis-scaled
# exponent moves them tens of kg apart.
stopifnot(all(abs(eff$`Weight implied by CL (kg)` / eff$`Weight implied by Vc (kg)` - 1) < 0.05))
```

# Linear and saturable clearance

At concentrations well below Km the saturable pathway clears Vmax / Km =
`r signif(exp(ini_vals[["lvmax"]] - ini_vals[["lkm"]]), 3)` L/day, about twenty
times the linear clearance, which is the paper's statement that "nonlinear
elimination is the dominant clearance pathway at lower concentrations"
(Discussion).

```{r clearance, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = "Typical linear, saturable and total clearance against serum natalizumab concentration for a 70-kg patient."}
cl_conc <- tibble(conc = 10^seq(-2, 2.2, length.out = 200)) |>
  mutate(
    Linear = exp(ini_vals[["lcl"]]),
    Saturable = exp(ini_vals[["lvmax"]]) / (exp(ini_vals[["lkm"]]) + conc),
    Total = Linear + Saturable
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-conc, names_to = "pathway", values_to = "cl")

ggplot(cl_conc, aes(conc, cl, linetype = pathway)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(2, 10), colour = "grey60") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Natalizumab concentration (ug/mL)", y = "Clearance (L/day)", linetype = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Virtual cohort

Observed data are not public. The virtual cohort draws body weight from a
normal distribution with the published median (73 kg) and a standard
deviation that reproduces the published IQR (64-83 kg), truncated to
40-140 kg. Between-subject random effects are drawn in base R from the
published variances so that each virtual patient keeps the same individual
parameters across every dosing interval simulated below, which is what the
paper's MIPD analysis does with its empirical Bayes estimates.

Each patient receives 300 mg as a 1-h IV infusion (infusion duration is not
stated in the paper; 1 h is the labelled duration) for 20 doses at each whole-
week interval from 4 to 12 weeks, which brings every interval to steady state
(the terminal half-life of the linear pathway is about a month). Concentrations
are recorded daily over the last interval and 1 h after the end of the last
infusion (the paper's peak sampling time).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2025)
n_sub <- 200
n_dose <- 20
intervals_wk <- 4:12

omega <- c(etalcl = 0.050678, etalvp = 0.094605, etalvmax = 0.065413)
stopifnot(all(abs(omega - diag(rxode2::rxode(mod)$omega)[names(omega)]) < 1e-9))

wt_sd <- (83 - 64) / (2 * qnorm(0.75))
patients <- tibble(
  patient = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_sub, 73, wt_sd), 40), 140),
  etalcl = rnorm(n_sub, 0, sqrt(omega[["etalcl"]])),
  etalvp = rnorm(n_sub, 0, sqrt(omega[["etalvp"]])),
  etalvmax = rnorm(n_sub, 0, sqrt(omega[["etalvmax"]]))
)

# One rxode2 subject per patient x interval; ids ascend so the params rows
# below line up with the subjects (rxSolve matches params rows by position).
design <- tidyr::expand_grid(interval_wk = intervals_wk, patient = patients$patient) |>
  left_join(patients, by = "patient") |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), tau = 7 * interval_wk)

make_events <- function(id, tau, WT) {
  last <- (n_dose - 1) * tau
  dose <- tibble(
    id = id, time = (seq_len(n_dose) - 1) * tau, evid = 1L, amt = 300,
    rate = 300 * 24, cmt = "central"
  )
  obs <- tibble(
    id = id, time = sort(unique(c(last + 0:tau, last + 2 / 24))), evid = 0L,
    amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central"
  )
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |> mutate(WT = WT)
}

events <- bind_rows(Map(make_events, design$id, design$tau, design$WT)) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
params <- design |> select(etalcl, etalvp, etalvmax)
# All randomness (weights, etas, residual draws) comes from base R, so the
# cohort is identical on every machine. The random effects enter through
# `params`; rxode2's "multi-subject simulation without omega" warning for the
# zeroRe() model is therefore expected and silenced.
sim <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = events, params = params,
  returnType = "data.frame"
)) |>
  left_join(design |> select(id, patient, interval_wk, tau), by = "id") |>
  mutate(tad = time - (n_dose - 1) * tau)

# Residual-error draw (proportional, 22% CV) for the "observed" troughs.
troughs <- sim |>
  filter(tad == tau) |>
  select(id, patient, interval_wk, ipred = Cc) |>
  arrange(id) |>
  mutate(obs = ipred * (1 + ini_vals[["propSd"]] * rnorm(n())))
```

# Steady-state troughs against Table S1

Table S1 reports the median (IQR) trough at the standard 4-week interval as
22 (15-33) ug/mL. The extended-interval troughs (median 9.9 ug/mL at a median
of 42 days, and 7.6 ug/mL in the NEXTMS low arm, also at 42 days) come from
patients whose interval was extended *because* their 4-week troughs were high,
so an unselected virtual cohort dosed every 6 weeks should sit below them; they
are shown for orientation and are not a gate.

```{r trough-table}
trough_summary <- troughs |>
  filter(interval_wk %in% c(4, 6)) |>
  group_by(interval_wk) |>
  summarise(
    median = median(obs),
    q25 = quantile(obs, 0.25),
    q75 = quantile(obs, 0.75),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    published = c("22 (15-33)", "9.9 (6.9-14); selected patients"),
    simulated = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)", median, q25, q75)
  )
trough_summary |>
  select(interval_wk, simulated, published) |>
  rename(
    "Interval (weeks)" = interval_wk,
    "Simulated trough, median (IQR), ug/mL" = simulated,
    "Table S1 trough, median (IQR), ug/mL" = published
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

# A mis-transcribed CL, Vmax, Km or volume moves the 4-week median trough by
# far more than this; the 25% envelope admits cohort-to-cohort noise and the
# fact that the published median pools three studies.
stopifnot(abs(trough_summary$median[1] / 22 - 1) < 0.25)
```

```{r trough-by-interval, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = "Simulated steady-state troughs (with residual error) by dosing interval. Grey lines mark the 10, 5 and 2 ug/mL targets of the paper."}
ggplot(troughs, aes(factor(interval_wk), obs)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(10, 5, 2), colour = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Dosing interval (weeks)", y = "Steady-state trough (ug/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# PKNCA validation

PKNCA is run on the final (steady-state) interval of the 4- and 6-week
regimens. The paper reports no NCA, so the comparison table uses the only
summary it gives: the median trough (`cmin`) at the standard interval and the
selected extended-interval median from Table S1. `ncaComparisonTable()` pools
by the median.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(interval_wk %in% c(4, 6), !is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste0("Q", interval_wk, "W")) |>
  select(id, treatment, tad, Cc)

dose_nca <- sim_nca |>
  distinct(id, treatment) |>
  mutate(tad = 0, amt = 300)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ tad | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ tad | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = c(28, 42), treatment = c("Q4W", "Q6W"),
  cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
knitr::kable(summary(nca_res), caption = "Steady-state NCA over the final dosing interval (geometric mean and CV unless stated).")

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmin,
  "Q4W",      22,
  "Q6W",      9.9
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", cmin = "ug/mL", auclast = "day*ug/mL", cav = "ug/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated steady-state NCA (median) vs. Table S1 trough medians. * differs from reference by >20%.")
```

The 4-week `cmin` agrees with the Table S1 median. The 6-week row is expected
to differ: the published value describes patients selected for extension by
high 4-week troughs, while every virtual patient here is extended regardless.
The NEXTMS protocol, for example, put a patient on a 6-week interval only after
two 4-week troughs of at least 30 ug/mL (main arm) or 25 ug/mL (low arm).

# Model-informed interval selection (Figure 3)

The paper simulated four MIPD algorithms on the NEXTMS patients, choosing for
each patient the whole-week interval whose individual predicted trough is
closest (on the log scale) to the target; algorithms 1 and 3 accept only
intervals whose predicted trough stays at or above the target. The same rules
are applied here to the individual predicted troughs of the virtual cohort,
with intervals limited to 4-12 weeks.

```{r mipd}
algorithms <- tibble(
  algorithm = c("A1", "A2", "A3", "A4"),
  target = c(5, 5, 2, 2),
  constrained = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE)
)

pick_interval <- function(ipred, interval_wk, target, constrained) {
  dist <- abs(log(ipred) - log(target))
  ok <- if (constrained) ipred >= target else rep(TRUE, length(ipred))
  if (!any(ok)) {
    return(min(interval_wk))
  }
  interval_wk[ok][which.min(dist[ok])]
}

chosen <- tidyr::expand_grid(algorithms, patient = patients$patient) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(interval_wk = {
    p <- troughs[troughs$patient == patient, ]
    pick_interval(p$ipred, p$interval_wk, target, constrained)
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  left_join(troughs |> select(patient, interval_wk, ipred, obs), by = c("patient", "interval_wk"))

mipd_summary <- chosen |>
  group_by(algorithm, target, constrained) |>
  summarise(
    mean_interval_wk = mean(interval_wk),
    infusions_pppy = mean(52 / interval_wk),
    pct_obs_below_target = 100 * mean(obs < target),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(reduction_pct = 100 * (1 - infusions_pppy / 13))
mipd_summary |>
  rename(
    "Algorithm" = algorithm,
    "Target (ug/mL)" = target,
    "Limit constrained" = constrained,
    "Mean interval (weeks)" = mean_interval_wk,
    "Infusions per person-year" = infusions_pppy,
    "Simulated troughs below target (%)" = pct_obs_below_target,
    "Reduction vs. 4-weekly (%)" = reduction_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

```{r figure-3a, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3A of van den Berg 2025: share of the population on each personalised interval under algorithms A1-A4."}
chosen |>
  count(algorithm, interval_wk) |>
  group_by(algorithm) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(interval_wk), pct, fill = algorithm)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(preserve = "single")) +
  labs(x = "Personalised interval (weeks)", y = "Population (%)", fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r figure-3b, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3B of van den Berg 2025: simulated observed troughs at the personalised interval under each algorithm."}
ggplot(chosen, aes(algorithm, obs)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(5, 2, 1), colour = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Simulated trough (ug/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

The paper reports that algorithm 3 (2 ug/mL target, limit constrained) reduces
infusions by 39% to about eight per person-year, with intervals of 4-10 weeks
(average about 7 weeks) and 11% of patients with simulated observed troughs
below 2 ug/mL, and that algorithm 2 (5 ug/mL target) reduces infusions by 35%.

```{r mipd-check}
a2 <- mipd_summary[mipd_summary$algorithm == "A2", ]
a3 <- mipd_summary[mipd_summary$algorithm == "A3", ]
# Means and shares over 200 patients; a mis-specified clearance pathway shifts
# the chosen intervals by whole weeks and the reductions by well over 10 points.
stopifnot(
  abs(a3$reduction_pct - 39) < 10,
  abs(a2$reduction_pct - 35) < 10,
  abs(a3$mean_interval_wk - 7) < 1,
  abs(a3$pct_obs_below_target - 11) < 8
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Infusion duration.** Not stated in the paper; 1 h (the labelled duration
  of the 300 mg infusion) is used. Steady-state troughs are insensitive to it.
- **Virtual cohort.** Body weight is drawn from a normal distribution matched
  to the Table 1 median and IQR; no other covariate enters the model. The
  paper's MIPD analysis used empirical Bayes estimates of real patients
  fitted to two 4-week troughs, whereas this vignette draws individual
  parameters from the population distribution. Because shrinkage on Vp and
  Vmax was high (66.7% and 35%), the paper's individual estimates are less
  dispersed than the population draws, so the interval distributions in
  Figure 3A are only approximately reproduced.
- **Residual error on the MIPD troughs.** The paper drew "observed" troughs by
  multiplying predictions by a sampled log prediction-to-observation ratio
  (mean 0.02, SD 0.32; Figure S7). The model's own 22% proportional error is
  used here instead.
- **Clearance units in the text.** The Results compare the final clearance
  with an earlier model as "0.164 vs. 0.15 L/h"; Table 2, Table S4 and the
  NONMEM code all give clearance in L/day, which is used.
- **Extended-interval comparison.** The 6-week rows of the trough and NCA
  tables are expected to fall below Table S1 because the published
  extended-interval patients were selected for high troughs (see above).
- No erratum or correction notice was found for this article (checked
  2026-11-04).
